cohort: The study included 268 postpartum women, aged 15-49 years, who had either a spontaneous vaginal delivery or a cesarean section, and were between six weeks and six months postpartum.
finding: Maternal health-related quality of life in postpartum women was moderately affected, with physical and social functioning domains contributing to better quality of life, while energy/fatigue, body pain, and general health were the weakest domains; poorer HRQOL was associated with the subacute postpartum phase, cesarean section, lower maternal education, and fewer antenatal visits.
mod_finding: Women who had a cesarean section were associated with poorer health-related quality of life.
